That is above the 20-40 target, but the verifier's list was adopted in full because each entry is a leading authority the earlier brief discussed only through later cases.

Added Rocka v. Roanoke County Department of Public Welfare (215 Va. 515) for INP-05, ACT-03, OUT-01: it is the pre-§ 16.1-283 rule Knox, Weaver, Toombs and Harris all argue about — in a parent versus non-parent contest the comparative-best-interests rule does not apply and the non-parent must prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence — and it arises from a mother who herself asked the board to place her children in foster care.

Added Berrien v. Greene County Department of Public Welfare (216 Va. 241) for ACT-02, OUT-01, OUT-05: it reaffirms Rocka, holds that a supported best-interests finding does not substitute for proof of unfitness, and restores custody to the mother by final judgment rather than remand. Note the correct party name is 'Department of Public Welfare', not 'Department of Social Services' as the verifier's list styled it.

Added Shank v. Department of Social Services (217 Va. 506) for INP-12, ACT-03, ACT-04: it is the Supreme Court of Virginia's definition of what a permanent-separation commitment order actually does, distinguishing a commitment that merely suspends custody from one that severs all parental rights and renders the parent 'a legal stranger to the child'.

Added Malpass v. Morgan (213 Va. 393) for OUT-02, OUT-03, OUT-05: it is the controlling Virginia condition on adoption over a natural parent's objection — parental rights may not be lightly severed — and the doctrinal predecessor of Doe v. Doe and Copeland v. Todd.

Added Kaywood v. Halifax County Department of Social Services (10 Va. App. 535) for ACT-01, ACT-06, OUT-06: it supplies the prospective 'within a reasonable time' framework and holds that the statutory prima facie triggers, including the offer of rehabilitative services, are not the exclusive route to a subsection (B) termination.

Added Toms v. Hanover Department of Social Services (46 Va. App. 257) for ACT-01, ACT-02: it is the opinion Yafi quotes for the governing subsection (C) rule and it draws the (B)/(C) line — services are a relevant factor under (B) but the measure of the parent's failure under (C). Note the case is styled 'Toms v. Hanover Department of Social Services' in the cluster, without 'County'.

Added Fields v. Dinwiddie County Department of Social Services (46 Va. App. 1) for ACT-02: its own holding is that under Code § 16.1-283(E)(i) a prior termination of rights to a sibling substitutes for proof that the parent failed to remedy the conditions, so the service record drops out of the case.

Added Jenkins v. Winchester Department of Social Services (12 Va. App. 1178) for INP-07, INP-12, DEC-04, DEC-05: its own holding is that the statutory definitions of an abused or neglected child require no proof of harm already suffered, because 'substantial risk' speaks in futuro and Code § 16.1-251(A)(1) authorizes removal of a newborn from the hospital before the child enters the dangerous environment.

Added Logan v. Fairfax County Department of Human Development (13 Va. App. 123) for ACT-04, ACT-06: its own holding is that the Department, not the parent, must produce sufficient evidence of willing and suitable relatives under Code § 16.1-283(A), and that a parent retains standing to contest the placement entered with the termination order.

Added James v. Jane (221 Va. 43) for FAIL-04, PMC-02: it is the four-factor test Messina v. Burden applies, holding state-employee immunity qualified rather than absolute and turning on the function performed, the state's interest and involvement in it, and the degree of state control.

Added Watson v. Shepard (217 Va. 538) for INP-05, ACT-04: it is the custody-order burden-shifting rule Walker exists to distinguish — a prior order entered after voluntary relinquishment, investigation and hearing puts the burden of showing changed circumstances on the parent and imposes no unfitness burden on the custodians — and it reversed the kinship adoption because the aunt and uncle were separating.

Added Vosburg v. Department Of Social Services (884 F.2d 133) for DEC-02, DEC-05, FAIL-02, FAIL-04: it is the Fourth Circuit predicate for Wildauer, Hodge and Martin. Its actual holding is stronger than the verifier's description: Virginia social workers have ABSOLUTE immunity for the prosecutorial act of filing a removal petition, and the Court expressly declined to extend that immunity to investigative conduct, which retains only qualified immunity.

Added Stadter v. Siperko (52 Va. App. 81) for ACT-04, OUT-03: relied on by name in Mast v. A.A., it declines to adopt a de facto or psychological parent doctrine in Virginia and holds a non-parent must overcome the Troxel presumption by proving actual harm before any best-interests analysis applies.

Added Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians v. Holyfield (490 U.S. 30) for INP-11, FAIL-03: INP-11 was the only node in the reconciled brief carrying fewer than two cases. Targeted searches of va and vactapp again returned no Virginia state-court decision applying ICWA, so the node is completed with the U.S. Supreme Court standard — domicile under § 1911(a) is uniform federal law and a state decree entered without ICWA jurisdiction must be vacated under 25 U.S.C. § 1914.

Citation correction: the verifier's list gives James v. Jane as '221 Va. 43, 267 S.E.2d 108 (1980)'. The CourtListener cluster (1275911, date_filed 1980-06-06) reports the parallel citation as 282 S.E.2d 864, and that is what is asserted here. Counsel checking the bound volumes should be aware of the discrepancy.

Quote-sourcing caveat on the two standard-of-review authorities. The phrases the verifier associated with Logan ('plainly wrong or without evidence to support it') and with Fields (the best-interests factor list) appear in those opinions only as quotations of Peple v. Peple, Barkey v. Commonwealth and Logan itself. Under the law-firm rule against quoting a court's restatement of a prior case, neither phrase could be used. Each entry instead quotes that court's own holding — Logan on the Department's duty to evaluate relatives, Fields on the § 16.1-283(E)(i) sibling-termination element.

Node-capacity note. DEC-03 (substantiated finding) and FAIL-01 (court reversal of agency decision) were already carrying the maximum of six cases before this pass, so several of the added authorities that also bear on those decision points — Rocka, Berrien, Malpass, Jenkins and Logan, all of which reverse or affirm on sufficiency grounds — could not be mapped there. Their relevance to FAIL-01 should be read out of their holdings even though the node map does not list them.

Coverage check after this pass: all 42 nodes carry between 2 and 6 cases; 51 distinct cases are used; every added case was retrieved from CourtListener in this session, its full opinion text read, and its quote machine-verified as an exact substring of the majority opinion (positional check confirms each quote precedes any dissent or concurrence in the retrieved text).

Missing (for a later pass): Santosky v. Kramer, 455 U.S. 745 (1982) — the constitutional floor the whole OUT-02 / Christopher Farrell line rests on: due process requires at least clear and convincing evidence before a State may sever parental rights. The brief mentions Santosky in passing in a note about ICWA standards but never cites it as an authority, which is a serious omission from a termination brief.

Missing (for a later pass): Troxel v. Granville, 530 U.S. 57 (2000) — the fit-parent presumption. Stadter is mapped and quoted for 'the constitutional concerns inherent in the Troxel presumption' while Troxel itself is absent; ACT-04 and OUT-03 cannot be briefed without it.

Missing (for a later pass): Lassiter v. Department of Social Services, 452 U.S. 18 (1981) — whether and when due process requires appointed counsel for an indigent parent at a termination hearing. Nothing in the brief addresses the parent's right to counsel at any decision point.

Missing (for a later pass): Stanley v. Illinois, 405 U.S. 645 (1972) — the foundational holding that a parent is entitled to a hearing on fitness before children are taken; the doctrinal root of DEC-04, DEC-05 and OUT-02.

Missing (for a later pass): Bottoms v. Bottoms, 249 Va. 410, 457 S.E.2d 102 (1995) — the Supreme Court of Virginia's later, materially qualifying treatment of a lesbian mother's custody, reversing the Court of Appeals and upholding transfer of custody to the grandmother. FAIL-05 currently presents Doe v. Doe as 'controlling' on status-based disqualification without this case; that is misleading and must be corrected.

Missing (for a later pass): Roe v. Roe, 228 Va. 722, 324 S.E.2d 691 (1985) — the companion Supreme Court of Virginia decision on a homosexual father's custody, decided between Doe and Bottoms; required to state the actual Virginia rule for FAIL-05.

Missing (for a later pass): Wilkerson v. Wilkerson, 214 Va. 395, 200 S.E.2d 581 (1973) — the parent/non-parent rule ('clear and convincing evidence, both that the parent is unfit and that the best interest of the child will be promoted') that Rocka and Berrien both quote by name and build on; INP-05, ACT-04 and OUT-01 rest on it.

Missing (for a later pass): Bailes v. Sours, 231 Va. 96, 340 S.E.2d 824 (1986) — the modern Supreme Court of Virginia statement of the parental presumption in a parent versus non-parent custody contest and how it is rebutted; the bridge between the 1970s Rocka/Berrien line and Copeland/Stadter.

Missing (for a later pass): Farley v. Farley, 9 Va. App. 326, 387 S.E.2d 794 (1990) — the 'past actions and relationships over a meaningful period serve as good indicators of what the future may be expected to hold' formulation quoted throughout the Virginia termination line; directly supports the prospective judgment framework the brief credits to Kaywood alone.

Missing (for a later pass): Ferguson v. Stafford County Department of Social Services, 14 Va. App. 333, 417 S.E.2d 1 (1992) — a leading Court of Appeals decision on § 16.1-283(C)(2) and the adequacy of the Department's rehabilitative efforts; ACT-01 and ACT-02 are thin without it.

Missing (for a later pass): Wright v. Alexandria Division of Social Services, 16 Va. App. 821, 433 S.E.2d 500 (1993) — the Court of Appeals' treatment of termination where a parent is incarcerated or otherwise unable to participate in services; Yafi is mapped for the incarcerated-parent point but Wright is the case that actually develops it.

Missing (for a later pass): Martin v. Pittsylvania County Department of Social Services, 3 Va. App. 15, 348 S.E.2d 13 (1986) — the Court of Appeals' first major § 16.1-283 opinion and the origin of much of the standard-of-review and best-interests language the later cases repeat; a termination brief that starts at Kaywood (1990) skips it.

Missing (for a later pass): Va. Code §§ 16.1-253 and 16.1-279.1 (preliminary and permanent protective orders) — not a case, but flagged because ACT-05 currently has no authority genuinely about protective orders; if no published Virginia opinion construes these provisions in the child-welfare context, the node should say so explicitly rather than stand on Jordan and Cook.
